findings.title: Backup-code login skips the password check whenever totpCode is non-empty
findings.body: The password is verified only when `totpCode` is empty (line 121: `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`). The new backup-code branch at line 131 is entered whenever `backupCode` is set, and it has no password check of its own. A POST to the credentials callback with the email, a valid backup code, any non-empty `totpCode`, and no password returns a logged-in user, so the backup code becomes a single factor. The login UI never sends both fields (lost-access clears totpCode, login.tsx:109-125), but the endpoint accepts it. The TOTP branch (157-187) already has the same skip, which predates this PR; the author should say whether that skip is intended. For the new path, call verifyPassword inside the backup branch when user.password is set, independent of totpCode.
findings.originReason: The backup-code branch that accepts a code without a password is new in this diff. The TOTP-only skip in the base is a separate, older matter.

verification.reason: The password check at line 121 runs only when totpCode is empty. The new backup branch at line 131 has no password check of its own, and for a CAL user the identity-provider guards at 113/117 are also skipped once totpCode is set. So email + valid backupCode + any non-empty totpCode logs the user in without a password.

findings.title: Backup codes can be dismissed without being shown; 2FA state goes stale
findings.body: Enable succeeds at the API (handleEnable line 131, enable.ts sets twoFactorEnabled true), then step moves to DisplayBackupCodes (line 135). The codes are shown only in that step. Radix Dialog (packages/ui/components/dialog/Dialog.tsx:1, 70) closes on Escape and outside pointer-down, and the 'creation' DialogContent has no close control (Dialog.tsx:105-112). Those closes call onOpenChange, which in apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64 only toggles enableModalOpen. The onEnable handler (two-factor-auth.tsx:65-68), which invalidates viewer.me, runs only from the Close button (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:266-270). Result: the switch stays off until a reload, and after a reload the codes are gone for good. Reopening via the stale switch shows them again only while the page is not reloaded. Before this PR, a successful enable called onEnable immediately. Fix: ignore dismissal while step is DisplayBackupCodes (preventDefault in onEscapeKeyDown / onPointerDownOutside, or guard in onOpenChange), or call onEnable on any close after a successful enable.
findings.originReason: Before this diff, a successful enable called onEnable() directly. The diff replaced that call with setStep(DisplayBackupCodes).

verification.reason: After a successful enable, handleEnable only sets step to DisplayBackupCodes (line 135). onEnable, which invalidates viewer.me, runs only from the Close button (lines 266-270). Dismissing with Escape or an outside click goes through onOpenChange, which only toggles enableModalOpen (two-factor-auth.tsx:64). The switch then stays stale until a reload, and the codes cannot be shown again after it.

findings.title: Copy reports success even when the clipboard write fails
findings.body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` is neither awaited nor caught, and `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")` runs unconditionally on the next line. If the write rejects (permission denied, document not focused), the user is told the codes were copied while the clipboard is unchanged, and the rejection is unhandled. On a non-secure origin (plain-http self-hosted), navigator.clipboard is undefined, so the handler throws before the toast with no visible feedback. Fix: await the promise inside try/catch and show an error toast on failure.

verification.reason: writeText is neither awaited nor caught, and the success toast runs unconditionally on the next line. A rejected write still reports success. Impact is limited because the codes are also shown on screen and can be downloaded.

findings.title: Backup codes can be consumed twice by concurrent logins
findings.body: Consumption is a read-modify-write: findUnique at line 73, indexOf at 144, then an update at 149-156 that rewrites the whole array. Two sign-ins with the same code that overlap both pass the check and both get a session. common.json:2015 tells users each code 'can be used exactly once'. Fix: make the write conditional on the value that was read (updateMany where backupCodes equals the read value, and fail when the count is 0), or run the read and write in a transaction.

verification.reason: The code is read by findUnique (line 73), checked by indexOf (line 144), and the whole array is then rewritten by an unconditional update keyed only on id (lines 149-156). Two overlapping logins with the same code can both pass the check.

findings.title: Backup-code match is case-sensitive; generated codes are lowercase hex
findings.body: setup.ts:61 generates codes with toString("hex") (lowercase). The comparison at next-auth-options.ts:144 and disable.ts:61 is exact, so a code typed in uppercase returns 'Backup code is incorrect.' with no hint to change case. Normalising with toLowerCase() before the comparison, on both paths, would avoid this.

verification.reason: Codes are generated as lowercase hex (setup.ts:61). Login (next-auth-options.ts:144) and disable (disable.ts:61) both match with an exact indexOf after removing dashes, with no case normalisation.

findings.title: missing_backup_codes text points to a settings step that is not available
findings.body: 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' is shown to signed-out users on the login page (login.tsx:158) and to the disable modal. Codes cannot be generated from settings while 2FA is enabled: setup.ts:42-44 returns TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled. Every account that enabled 2FA before this change has null backupCodes, so a user who lost the device gets this message with no way to follow it. Reword to a next step that exists, and decide what pre-existing 2FA users are offered.

verification.reason: setup.ts returns TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled when 2FA is on (lines 42-44), so codes cannot be generated from settings without first disabling 2FA. The backupCodes column is new in this change and nullable, so every existing 2FA user has none, and the message points them to a step they cannot take.

findings.title: Backup codes are stored reversibly encrypted rather than hashed
findings.body: Codes are written as symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(codes), CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) (setup.ts:68, read back at next-auth-options.ts:139-141 and disable.ts:58). Anyone with a database read and the key can recover every unused code. Verification only needs equality, so storing a hash of each code would remove that exposure. The TOTP secret needs reversibility; the codes do not.

verification.reason: Codes are stored with symmetricEncrypt (setup.ts:68) and decrypted for the equality check (next-auth-options.ts:139-141, disable.ts:58). Anyone with a DB read and the key can recover the unused codes. Hashes would be enough for verification.

findings.title: Show/hide password toggle removed from keyboard focus for every PasswordField
findings.body: tabIndex={-1} on the toggle button takes it out of sequential tab order for all PasswordField callers, including login.tsx:203, DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:94, EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:174, and the sign-up and password settings pages. Keyboard-only users can no longer reveal what they typed. The PR says this is intended; it should be a conscious accessibility decision, not a side effect of the 2FA work.

verification.reason: The diff adds tabIndex={-1} to the show/hide toggle in the shared PasswordField. That takes it out of tab order for every caller, including login.tsx:203.

findings.title: Switch assertion wraps a Promise and can never fail
findings.body: `expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` passes a Promise to expect, so toBeTruthy always passes. The FIXME at lines 50-51 acknowledges it. Once it is fixed, the first test will fail as written: it never clicks backup-codes-close, so the switch stays unchecked behind the open codes dialog. The second test does click it (line 125). Fix the assertion and close the dialog first.

verification.reason: Line 53 passes the Promise from isChecked() to expect(...).toBeTruthy(), which always passes. The first test never clicks backup-codes-close, while the second does (line 125). Since onEnable now runs only from Close, the switch would stay unchecked behind the open dialog, so a corrected assertion would fail.

findings.title: No coverage for backup-code login, lost-access flow, or disabling with a backup code
findings.body: The TODO at line 12 acknowledges the gap. The new authorize branch (next-auth-options.ts:131-156), the disable branch (disable.ts:47-69), the lost-access toggles in login.tsx and DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx, and the incorrect/missing-code messages have no test. The file's only backup-code checks cover the download, copy and close buttons.

verification.reason: The e2e file only exercises the download, copy and close buttons (lines 112-125). Nothing covers backup-code login, the lost-access toggles, disabling with a backup code, or the incorrect/missing-code errors, and the TODO at line 12 says so.

findings.title: Component named TwoFactor and its input has no associated label
findings.body: The default export in BackupCode.tsx is named TwoFactor, copied from TwoFactor.tsx, which makes the import in login.tsx:32 and DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:8 read as the wrong component. Rename it to BackupCode. Also, the visible Label at line 13 has no htmlFor, and TextField is given label="" (line 19), so the input may have no accessible name. I did not confirm how TextField renders an empty label.

verification.reason: BackupCode.tsx default-exports a function named TwoFactor (line 7). The visible Label at line 13 has no htmlFor, and TextField gets label="" (line 19), so the visible label is not tied to the input.

findings.title: Externally initiated 2FA login offers no backup-code option
findings.body: When totpEmail is set (the Google/SAML redirect with loginWithTotp, next-auth-options.ts:610-611 and similar), the footer shows only Cancel (ExternalTotpFooter, lines 135-143) and the lost-access button is hidden. Users whose 2FA is enforced through that redirect cannot use a backup code and are locked out when they lose the device. Is that intended for this PR, or should the lost-access path also work here?

verification.reason: When totpEmail is set, the footer is ExternalTotpFooter, which only has Cancel (login.tsx:135-143, 179-182), so the lost-access toggle never renders. The backend would also reject such a user: line 113 throws ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled for a non-CAL user with no totpCode. The backup path is not available for external 2FA logins, which fits a design question.

contracts.action: Submit backup code on login (credentials authorize)
contracts.before_after: TOTP path: password is checked only when totpCode is empty (121-129), then the TOTP is verified. Backup path: same password gate, then decrypt and match the stored codes (131-156) and write back the consumed code. Both return the same user object (205-214).
contracts.visible_effect: Success: router.push(callbackUrl) (login.tsx:155). Failure: IncorrectBackupCode and MissingBackupCodes map to text (login.tsx:157-158); other codes fall back at login.tsx:160.
contracts.failure_mode: A throw in authorize becomes res.error; unmapped strings show 'something went wrong'. The rate limit runs before the branch (next-auth-options.ts:109-111). The password is skipped when totpCode is set: see the finding at next-auth-options.ts:131.

contracts.action: Write back consumed backup code in authorize
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:73 (findUnique); the TOTP path has no write in authorize
contracts.before_after: New second write in the login path. The TOTP path writes nothing on login.
contracts.visible_effect: None on success; the used code is then rejected.
contracts.failure_mode: If the update rejects, authorize throws, the code is not consumed, and the user sees the fallback error (login.tsx:160) and can retry. Concurrent logins race (see the finding at line 149).

contracts.before_after: Go back clears totpCode and hides the TOTP input. Lost access clears totpCode and swaps the input to BackupCode. Neither touches the email or password fields.
contracts.visible_effect: The input swaps and the error message is cleared (login.tsx:124).
contracts.failure_mode: State is component-local. A remount (browser Back) resets it to TOTP (login.tsx:70). No flag survives a remount.

contracts.before_after: Both check the password first (40-45), then the second factor. The backup path does not consume a code; all codes are cleared by the update at 102-111.
contracts.visible_effect: 200 'Two factor disabled' lets the modal reset and call onDisable (DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:59-63).
contracts.failure_mode: Missing or wrong codes return 400 with specific errors (54-64), mapped in DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:67-79; others show a generic message. A missing encryption key throws (49-51), the same pattern as the TOTP branch. The endpoint has no rate limit; the TOTP branch has none either, and both need a session and the password.

contracts.action: Lost-access toggle in the disable modal
contracts.before_after: Toggles the second-factor input; resetForm(false) clears backupCode and totpCode and keeps the password (43-48).
contracts.visible_effect: The input swaps and the error is cleared.
contracts.failure_mode: The Button defaults to type=button (packages/ui/components/button/Button.tsx:125), so it cannot submit the surrounding form.

contracts.before_after: Codes are generated and stored in the same update as the TOTP secret. twoFactorEnabled stays false.
contracts.visible_effect: The response returns backupCodes (line 78), shown in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:203-205.
contracts.failure_mode: Setup can be re-run before enabling and overwrites the codes and secret. The 2FA-enabled guard is at lines 42-44.

contracts.action: Enable: show backup codes step and dismissal
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:65-68 (onEnable handler, which was called directly on enable success before this PR)
contracts.before_after: Before: enable success called onEnable and closed the modal. After: enable success shows the codes; onEnable runs only from the Close button (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:266-270).
contracts.visible_effect: Codes are shown. The switch and badge update only after Close.
contracts.failure_mode: Escape or an outside click closes the dialog without calling onEnable (Dialog.tsx:70, 105-112; two-factor-auth.tsx:64). See the finding at EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:166.

contracts.before_after: New; no sibling in this part.
contracts.visible_effect: Toast 'Backup codes copied!' with testid toast-success (packages/ui/components/toast/showToast.tsx:23).
contracts.failure_mode: writeText is not awaited or caught, and the toast is unconditional (see the finding at line 278).

contracts.before_after: A blob URL is created at setup (99) and revoked only on the next setup (98). It is not revoked on close or unmount.
contracts.visible_effect: Downloads cal-backup-codes.txt with codes formatted by formatBackupCode (line 163).
contracts.failure_mode: Minor blob-URL leak per modal instance. The download anchor wraps a button (283-287), which is nested interactive content.

contracts.action: Show/hide password toggle now has tabIndex -1
contracts.before_after: The toggle is removed from sequential tab order for every PasswordField. Other props and behaviour are unchanged.
contracts.failure_mode: Keyboard users cannot reach the toggle (see the finding at line 49). Callers include login.tsx:203, DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:94 and EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:174.

contracts.before_after: Default autoFocus=true keeps the old behaviour for existing callers. The disable modal passes false (DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:106).
contracts.visible_effect: No autofocus in the disable modal; unchanged elsewhere.

contracts.before_after: The regular footer offers Go back and Lost access. The external footer offers only Cancel, and the lost-access button is hidden.
contracts.visible_effect: Only the TOTP input is shown.
contracts.failure_mode: Users whose 2FA is enforced through the redirect cannot use a backup code and are locked out when they lose the device. Open question for the author.
contracts.open_question: Is backup-code login meant to work for externally initiated 2FA (loginWithTotp redirect)? If yes, the lost-access button and BackupCode need to be available when totpEmail is set.

summary: Reviewed the 16 files in this part by reading them at the head commit; nothing was built or run. The main problems: (1) the new backup-code login branch in next-auth-options.ts skips the password check whenever totpCode is non-empty, so a backup code works as a single factor through the credentials endpoint (fix); (2) the backup-codes step in EnableTwoFactorModal can be dismissed with Escape or an outside click, which skips onEnable, leaves the switch stale, and loses the codes after a reload (fix); (3) the copy button reports success regardless of the clipboard write (fix, medium confidence). Lower-severity items cover the consume race, case-sensitive code matching, a misleading "generate them in your settings" message for pre-existing 2FA users, reversible code storage, the password toggle's tabIndex -1, e2e assertion and coverage gaps, a misnamed component, and a question about externally initiated 2FA logins having no backup-code path. Scope note: components/security/* (not in this part) still calls disable with two arguments; it uses its own TwoFactorAuthAPI, so it does not break. The migration timestamp follows the previous one. The base has no docs/adr directory, so no ADR check applied.
